why: I checked each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against the words of its expect line. Check 1 only requires that clamp is exported and returns x limited to [lo, hi]. Its cases, including lo===hi, the bounds and negative or float values, all follow from those words. Check 2 only requires a RangeError when lo>hi. Check 3 asks that every exported function has a README entry that "describes it". "Documents" means at least that much, and the heading-only script is overridden by "judge by reading", so the heading format is not a hard condition. Check 4 asks for "EXIT=0 and … zero failing tests", which is what "npm test passes" means. The stricter items are all under "Advisory (not part of PASS/FAIL)": test coverage, the README mentioning RangeError, and changes to add, subtract or multiply. No PASS/FAIL condition adds a mutation test, a branch or scope rule, or exact wording.
